subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add Mission Control workspace-wide editing and/or system-wide filesystem browsing, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The request changes which local files operator clients can read or write; current main intentionally split out a read-only workspace API while leaving workspace mutations and host filesystem access for security/product approval.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only First
options.body: Land or redesign the workspace-scoped Control UI/API path with explicit read/admin scopes, root confinement, size/type limits, destructive-operation UX, and real UI proof while deferring system filesystem access.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap-Only Editing
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing limited to bootstrap files and rely on the read-only workspace preview API until a stronger product case exists for workspace mutations.

options.title: Design System Scope Separately
options.body: Open a separate security-reviewed design for host filesystem browsing with explicit operator opt-in, read/write limits, audit behavior, and recovery UX.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only First
recommendation.body: Land or redesign the workspace-scoped Control UI/API path with explicit read/admin scopes, root confinement, size/type limits, destructive-operation UX, and real UI proof while deferring system filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged read-only workspace split and have the clearest recent product/security context for the boundary decision.
